one_month_reasoning: No CIFR earnings fall in the window: Q2 was reported Aug 4 and Q3 2025 was reported Nov 3, so Q3 2026 is most likely in the first week of November, just after Oct 31. Scheduled items inside the window: the Oct 28 FOMC (Kalshi hold 72.5c, hike 27.5c, $126K 24h volume as of Oct 1; Polymarket hike 24.5c, $235K 24h volume). A hold would be mildly good for long-duration, levered infrastructure names; a hike would hurt. Other possible news: a Barber Lake first rent-commencement notice (expected Q4, mostly priced in after the Sep 25 extension); the Google warrant exercise window opening at lease commencement, with a $430M value make-whole (shortfall about $56M at $15.46); ongoing V3 Holding disposals; and sector beta to the neocloud/AI-capex tape, which has been weak since July. With nothing decisive scheduled, I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred on $15.40 with a monthly sigma of 0.31 (112%/3.5), with a slight negative tilt from the supply overhang and the sector downtrend.

fair_value.method: Blend: asset DCF of the 3 executed hyperscale leases (8% discount rate, 6.75% exit cap, NOI $790M in 2028 rising to $894M in 2035) plus a $1.4B pipeline option = $10.2 (45%); 14x 2028E EBITDA = $8.5 (25%); analyst consensus $30.93 haircut 40% = $18.6 (30%). Result about $12.29. About $6B of debt against about $9B of contracted-asset EV leaves thin equity, so value is very sensitive to the cap rate and to pipeline leasing.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Asset-level DCF valued at 2027-10-01: NOI $640M (2027), $790M (2028) rising linearly to $894M (2035), $915M (2037); cash overhead $110M growing 3%; maintenance capex 2% of NOI; cash tax 0% to 2030 then 12% of CF; discount rate 8.0%; exit cap 6.75% on 2037 NOI (Barber Lake contracted to ~2046, AWS Black Pearl to ~2041). EV $8.92B -> equity $7.33/sh ex-pipeline; + pipeline option $1.40B ($2.87/sh) = $10.2. Sensitivity: 7.5-8.5% / 6.0-7.5% cap gives $6.8-$11.0 ex-pipeline+pipeline.

methods.inputs: Analyst consensus 12m target $30.93 (22 analysts) haircut 40% for documented target over-optimism, esp. for high-volatility small caps after a 50% drawdown.

bear.story: AI-capex digestion deepens (overspend fears, neocloud credit stress). Fluidstack-side risk or construction overruns at Barber Lake (Cipher bears the first $359M). ERCOT verification stalls the pipeline. Market values CIFR on contracted assets only at a 7.5%+ cap, giving about $5-8 of equity. A bitcoin slide (Polymarket gave about 23% to <$45k in 2026 as of Aug) hurts sentiment.

base.story: Black Pearl, Barber Lake and Stingray deliver roughly on time, and NOI ramps toward the $790M run-rate. One more mid-size lease (Stingray expansion/Odessa) is signed, but equity needs and a 5%+ 10Y cap the multiple. The stock trades about at today's level with high volatility, as peers did through the 2026 round trip.

bull.story: A large new hyperscale or AI-lab lease (Apollo 900 MW or Batch Zero capacity) at strong rents, the AI-infrastructure trade re-rates (as it did Apr-Jun 2026, when CIFR went from $12.9 to $30), and the market capitalises contracted NOI at core 5.5% cap rates. Consensus targets of about $31-35 are reached.

thesis_break_reason: At about $8 the market would be valuing CIFR below my ex-pipeline value of the contracted leases (about $7.3-8.3/sh at a 6.75-7.5% cap), assigning nothing to 4.4 GW of pipeline. That would most likely mean something fundamental went wrong: a tenant or backstop problem, a large overrun or delay at Barber Lake/Stingray, a forced equity raise, or a credit event in the AI-lab/neocloud chain, rather than ordinary 112%-vol noise.

reasoning: Base-rate anchor: CIFR's realized vol is 112%, and from Twelve Data monthly closes its own 12m log-return s.d. was about 1.0 (2021-26). Pooled CIFR/HUT/APLD 12m returns have q10 -49%, median +66%, q90 +238%, and after >=40% drawdowns from the 12m high the median forward return was +128% (n=40). But that sample is dominated by the 2023-25 bitcoin/AI bull run (strong survivorship and regime bias), so I take only the width and the fat right tail from it, not the drift. Peers (IREN, WULF, CORZ, APLD, HUT) all round-tripped in 2026: up 60-100% Apr-Jun, then down 35-50% Jul-Sep on AI-overspend fears, an IREN impairment, softer-than-whispered AI-lab ARR and higher long rates. CIFR is moving with the group (about -49% from its $30.14 high), so sector beta dominates. Fundamentals: three executed hyperscale leases (AWS x2, Fluidstack/Google, with Barber Lake now extended to 20 years) give about $793M average NOI, but there is about $6B of debt. An asset DCF at an 8% discount rate and a 6.75% exit cap gives about $7.3/sh before pipeline and about $10.2 with a $1.4B pipeline option. A 14x 2028E EBITDA multiple gives $8.5. Consensus is $30.93, haircut to $18.6 for target over-optimism. My blended fair value is about $12.3, below the $15.46 price: the market is effectively capitalising contracted NOI near core 5.5-6% cap rates and paying for pipeline. Macro/event odds: Kalshi shows no Fed cuts in 2026 and a ~27% chance of an Oct hike. Polymarket's bitcoin odds were bearish in Aug (BTC since recovered to about $85k). ERCOT's Batch Zero pause delays pipeline monetisation to 2027. Ladder: an 88/12 mixture of lognormals, the main one with median $15.5 and sigma 0.72 and a bust component with median $7 and sigma 0.6 (financing/tenant/AI-capex shock). That gives an overall median of about $14.1, below spot, reflecting fair value below price and the supply overhang, offset by rent commencement turning cash flow positive. P(>=15.46) is 0.45 and P(>=31) is 0.15. Research limits: Twelve Data statistics/targets and Alpha Vantage were plan- or rate-limited; Stooq and FRED were unreachable, so the 10Y came from Treasury.gov.
